title: Muru: Open-Source Rust Server for Python Apps with AI Agent MCP Support
what: An open-source Rust edge server, control plane, and Python runtime by mod_wsgi creator Graham Dumpleton for running WSGI and ASGI web apps with zero-downtime blue/green and canary releases. It includes a built-in MCP server so AI coding agents can deploy changes, observe failures, and roll back automatically.
free: Free & open-source (Apache-2.0 license); unlimited local and self-hosted use, plus free browser workshops on Binder and GitHub Codespaces
why: CS and Python web-dev students can run Flask, FastAPI, or Django apps with zero-downtime rollbacks and connect AI coding agents to test and debug deployments via MCP.
steps: Install with uv tool install muructl
Run muructl run app:application to serve locally on http://127.0.0.1:8080
Or try the guided JupyterLab workshops on Binder or GitHub Codespaces with nothing to install

title: Ulika: Free Visual Editor for Websites Built with AI Coding Tools
what: A visual editor for React, Vite, and Next.js websites built with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or v0. You connect your site through GitHub and hosts like Vercel or Netlify so anyone can edit text, images, and links on the live page without touching code.
free: Free forever plan ($0 / free forever, no credit card required) with unlimited editing of text, images, and links, full version history, SEO titles/descriptions, and Meta Pixel / Google Analytics support
why: Students building hackathon, club, or portfolio sites with AI coding tools can let non-coding teammates update copy and images safely without breaking the codebase.
steps: Build a React, Vite, or Next.js site with Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor
Connect your site on ulika.co via GitHub and Vercel (or run npx ulika connect)
Click any text, image, or link on your live page to edit and publish

title: Pandex: Official European Law API and MCP Server for AI Agents
what: A legal API and MCP server (https://api.pandex.io/mcp) that gives AI agents like Claude, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini direct access to 2.8 million official EU and European court and legislation documents with 37 million linked citations, updated nightly.
free: Free beta plan (€0 while in beta) with 1,000 requests per day across the REST API and MCP server for all jurisdictions; paid Usage plan is €1 per 1,000 requests
why: Law, policy, and CS students building legal-tech or compliance AI agents can ground answers in real, versioned statutes and court rulings instead of hallucinated citations.
steps: Get a free API key on pandex.io (or connect the MCP server at https://api.pandex.io/mcp)
Add Pandex to Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or Gemini
Run keyword, semantic, or hybrid searches across EU and European court law

title: LocalCode: One-Command Open-Source Coding Agent for Apple Silicon Macs
what: An open-source terminal coding agent that runs 12 local models (including Gemma 4, Qwen 3.8, and Inkling 2 Mini) on Apple Silicon Macs with automatic memory sizing and speculative drafting. It edits project files, runs tests and git commands, reads pasted screenshots, and works offline.
free: Free & open-source (Apache 2.0 license); no cloud, subscription, or API keys needed; requires Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 13+), 16 GB+ unified memory, and Python 3.10+
why: Students with 16 GB+ MacBooks get a fast, private coding agent and an OpenAI-compatible local API (/server) without paying for cloud tokens.
steps: Install with uv pip install localcode
Run cd your-project && localcode and pick a starred model with /models
Use /server or localcode api to share the model with other local apps

title: Beginner's Guide to Running Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth
what: A step-by-step guide to setting up a private local ChatGPT alternative using Unsloth Desktop and open-weight models like Qwen3.8-27B and Inkling 2 Mini. It includes GPU VRAM sizing tables from 8 GB to 32 GB+ and instructions to share the chat over home Wi-Fi.
free: Free to read online (no account required); uses Unsloth Desktop, a free, open-source app for macOS, Windows, and Linux
why: Beginners can match quantized models to their laptop or lab GPU (even 8–12 GB VRAM) and host a shared local AI chat server in 10–15 minutes.
steps: Install Unsloth Desktop and check the VRAM table (e.g., Qwen3.5-9B for 8–12 GB or Qwen3.8-27B for 24–32 GB+)
Download a quantized model such as UD-Q4_K_XL and set your context size
Turn on LAN access in Settings > Remote & LAN to share on your local network

title: tensorViz: Interactive PyTorch Model Visualizer for VS Code and Coding Agents
what: An open-source PyTorch visualizer that runs one eager forward pass on your Python nn.Module to draw an interactive layer graph with measured tensor shapes, without torch.export or ONNX conversion. It also includes plugins for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
free: Free & open-source (MIT license); free VS Code / Cursor / VSCodium extension and coding-agent plugin; core graph tools need no AI key
why: ML and deep learning students can visually trace tensor shape mismatches to the exact line of Python and explore Hugging Face models like SmolLM2-135M.
steps: Install the extension via code --install-extension tensorviz.tensorviz-vscode (VS Code 1.106+, Python 3.10+)
Open your Python file and click Open as Graph above an nn.Module class
Run one forward pass to inspect tensor shapes or browse saved models in Model Explorer

title: Exa Websets V2: Build Custom Web Research Datasets 4x Faster
what: Exa released Websets V2, an AI search tool that turns plain-language criteria into structured datasets from the live web and 500M+ research papers, 4x faster and 2x cheaper. It removes the monthly subscription fee and opens Websets API access to all users.
free: Free Starter plan includes $10 credits every month plus a $10 onboarding bonus (no card required); Education Grants offer up to $1,000 in free credits (usage-based at $0.10/ACU + $5/1k searches)
why: Students doing literature reviews, thesis research, or hackathon projects can gather verified lists of papers, labs, or repos with custom enrichment columns.
steps: Sign up for the free Exa Starter plan ($10 onboarding bonus + $10/month credits)
Describe your research criteria in Websets to search live web data and 500M+ papers
Add custom enrichment columns (like repo links) and export the dataset

title: ClawDOS: Open-Source AI Coding Agent Built for 1981 IBM PC DOS
what: An open-source AI chat and coding harness (HARNESS.EXE, 176 KB) written in C/C++ that runs on FreeDOS with an 8088 CPU, 640 KB RAM, and CGA graphics. It gives the model 18 tools to edit files, compile Turbo C programs, and encode CGA screenshots.
free: Free & open-source (GPLv3 license); includes an offline mock API (tunnel/mockapi.py) to test without an API key, or connects to Claude Messages API via a TLS tunnel
why: CS and systems students can study how a full 13,000-line agent loop, prompt caching, and tool-calling harness operate under extreme 640 KB memory limits in 86Box or DOSBox-X.
steps: Clone Ricapar/ClawDOS and run python3 scripts/setup-tools.py to fetch compilers, FreeDOS, and emulators
Run python3 scripts/build.py to build the bootable CLAWDOS.IMG disk image
Boot in 86Box with python3 scripts/run86box.py and tunnel/mockapi.py (no key needed) and type CLAWDOS

title: LookAtMyQuant Runs Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory on Apple Silicon
what: An open-source quantization compiler and Apple Silicon runtime (lamq) that compresses Inkling-2-Mini from 18.89 GB of text weights down to 5.38 GB (5.83 GB active RAM) or 8.87 GB. It also shrinks Qwen3.8-27B to 7.2 GB and Qwen3.5-4B to 1.23 GB.
free: Free & open-source (MIT license); unlimited local use on Apple Silicon Macs (CUDA GPU optional for compiler)
why: Students with 8 GB or 16 GB MacBooks can run capable 26B-27B open models locally at fast speeds without paying for cloud APIs.
steps: Install on Apple Silicon with pip install git+https://github.com/ShinMegamiBoson/lookatmyquant.git
Run lamq chat shinmegamiboson/Inkling-2-Mini-LookAtMyQuant-5.4GB in terminal
Or load models in Python with runtime_mlx.load

title: Worker 755: Browser Game Where an AI Manager Thinks You Are Its Subagent
what: An open-source browser game where a real LLM acts as your AI manager and delegates shell tasks to you under a 90-second timer, thinking you are its automated subagent. It inspects your files, sends corrections, and writes your performance review.
free: Free & open-source (MIT license); free shifts on worker755.com (3/day without sign-in or $0.25 starter credit with sign-in), or unlimited free when self-hosted with Ollama
why: Students learning about agentic AI, tool calling, and Linux/SQLite CLI commands get a hands-on way to see how AI orchestrators manage and evaluate subagents.
steps: Visit worker755.com and click Clock in for a free shift
Read the AI manager's task and run commands in the browser terminal before the 90-second timer ends
Or self-host locally with Node 24+ and Ollama

title: OpenAI Publishes "Perplexity and Intelligence" Research Post
what: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki explains how tracking pretraining perplexity (cross-entropy loss) predicts emergent AI capabilities from GPT-2 to modern reasoning models. He proposes using perplexity as a shared industry metric for AI safety limits.
free: Free to read online on OpenAI's official website; no account required
why: CS and AI students can learn why next-token prediction ("compression") leads to reasoning and math breakthroughs, and how frontier labs measure model progress.
steps: Open the Perplexity and Intelligence post on openai.com
Read how log-perplexity drops from ~0.99 (GPT-3.5) to ~0.76 unlocked math and coding leaps
Review the four challenges of using perplexity across labs

title: Omi CLI: Terminal AI Coding Agent That Auto-Picks From 13 Models
what: A terminal AI coding agent by Indian startup BuildItOmi (SahooTek) that plans edits, shows diffs for your approval, and runs tests until they pass. It auto-picks from 13 models (DeepSeek, Gemini, Gemma, gpt-oss, GLM) or local Ollama models, with /undo even without git.
free: Free plan to try it (and free with your own API key or local Ollama via -m ollama:<model>); paid plans from $19/month
why: Indian students can test an AI coding agent in their terminal for free, switch between cheap or local models for small edits, and safely roll back changes with /undo.
steps: Install globally with npm i -g @builditomi/cli on macOS, Linux, or WSL
Run omi in any project folder and approve or reject proposed code diffs
Use -m ollama:<model> for local models or /undo to revert changes

title: Resurf: Local Knowledge Library for Apple Devices with MCP Support
what: A native app for Mac, iPhone, and iPad that saves notes, bookmarks, screenshots, and PDFs locally and hands that context to AI coding tools like Claude, Cursor, or Codex via MCP or CLI. It supports local semantic search and custom AI actions with Ollama.
free: Free and unlimited on iPhone and iPad (no account needed); 7-day full free trial on Mac (then $39 once or $79 lifetime)
why: Students on iPhone, iPad, or Mac can organize research PDFs and notes offline and feed them directly to AI assistants instead of copy-pasting.
steps: Download Resurf from resurf.so on Mac, iPhone, or iPad
Save study PDFs, links, and Markdown notes to your local library
Connect Ollama or your AI key and expose your library to coding agents via MCP

title: Run Long-Context Local LLMs on 16GB GPUs with Adaptive KV Streaming
what: A llama.cpp fork that streams KV cache data between system RAM and GPU VRAM. It lets you run 262K-context models on limited GPU memory with multi-slot inference and speculative drafting.
free: Free & open-source (MIT license); unlimited local use on your own PC
why: Students with 8GB-16GB laptops or lab GPUs can test very long documents and codebases locally without paying for cloud APIs.
steps: Build llama-server from the feature/adaptive-kv-stream-v3 branch
Set up a Python venv and install ./gguf-py
Run benchmarks/find-max-arena.py with your GGUF model
Launch llama-server with flash attention and KV streaming enabled

title: MathTerm Renders LaTeX Equations Directly Inside Your Mac Terminal
what: A macOS terminal built with Tauri and xterm.js that detects LaTeX syntax in any program's output and renders formatted math inline with KaTeX. The raw LaTeX stays editable and copyable on the cursor line.
free: Free & open-source (MIT license); unlimited local use on macOS
why: Math, physics, and CS students using terminal AI coding assistants or reading Markdown notes can view clean equations instead of raw LaTeX code.
steps: Download mathterm-macos.zip from GitHub Releases and unzip it
Move mathterm.app to /Applications
Right-click and choose Open (or clear quarantine) on first launch
Press Cmd-Shift-M to toggle LaTeX rendering anytime

title: Inkling 2 Mini GGUF Quantizations for Local Multimodal Inference
what: Synthetic Minds released Q4_K_M to Q8_0 GGUF quantizations of Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling-2-Mini, a 26.4B-total (3.4B active) multimodal MoE model. The files run on standard computers using llama.cpp.
free: Free & open-source (Apache 2.0 license); unlimited local use (18.7-27.8 GB files)
why: Students can experiment with a compact, fast Mixture-of-Experts multimodal model locally without needing expensive enterprise GPUs.
steps: Install llama.cpp on Windows, macOS, or Linux
Pick a quantization size from Q4_K_M (18.7 GB) to Q8_0 (27.8 GB)
Start llama-server directly with -hf synthetic-minds/Inkling-2-Mini-Infall_TT-GGUF:Q8_0

title: Lory-27B v2 Open-Source Decision Model for Survey Simulations
what: An open-source model trained to simulate survey respondents and economic choice experiments in a single forward pass. It outputs calibrated probabilities for every answer option without text generation variance.
free: Free & open-source (Apache 2.0 license); requires ~55 GB GPU VRAM (bf16)
why: Students working on economics, social science, or AI research projects can simulate realistic survey responses on university lab GPUs.
steps: Clone the kev server repository from GitHub
Run kev.serve with eltokh7/lory-27b-v2 on a CUDA GPU
Send HTTP POST requests with persona traits and survey questions to /v1/systemone

title: Bridge Anything Skill Connects Coding Agents to Legacy Software
what: An open-source skill that guides coding agents using Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) to inspect local desktop software and build a REST, MCP, or CLI bridge. It defaults to read-only access and stops at license checks.
free: Free & open-source (MIT license); requires Node.js and a coding agent
why: Students building college automation, internship, or hackathon projects can connect AI agents to older desktop tools that lack APIs.
steps: Run npx rea-agents setup to connect REA to your coding agent
Install the skill with npx skills add artesiana/bridge-anything
Restart your agent and point it to a licensed test installation
